# Plan: Configurable Page Size for Submission Lists (#3045) ## Approach Add a per-source page-size preference stored in `localStorage`, surfaced as a small dropdown in `ShowCandidatesComponent`. The selected value feeds directly into the existing `this.pageSize` field that `performSearch()` already reads, so no new search path is needed. Note: both SavedList and SavedSearch currently default to 12 in `CandidateSourceBaseComponent.performSearch()` — there is no existing difference between them. Going forward we introduce that distinction as requested: | Source type | Options | Default | |-------------|---------|---------| | SavedList | 10, 25, 50, 100 | 10 | | SavedSearch | 25, 50, 100 | 25 | No backend changes required — `pageSize` is already part of every paged request (`PagedSearchRequest`). No virtual scroll, no infinite scroll; full-DOM rendering is acceptable up to 100 rows. --- ## Files That Change ### 1. `show-candidates.component.ts` **New constants / fields** ```typescript readonly listPageSizeOptions: number[] = [10, 25, 50, 100]; readonly searchPageSizeOptions: number[] = [25, 50, 100]; private readonly pageSizeSuffix: string = 'PageSize'; get pageSizeOptions(): number[] { return isSavedSearch(this.candidateSource) ? this.searchPageSizeOptions : this.listPageSizeOptions; } ``` The template uses `pageSizeOptions` unchanged; the getter returns the right set based on the current source type. **New private helpers** ```typescript /** * Returns the localStorage key used to persist the page-size preference * for the current candidate source. */ private pageSizeKey(): string { return getCandidateSourceType(this.candidateSource) + this.candidateSource.id + this.pageSizeSuffix; } /** * Reads the persisted page-size preference for the current source and * applies it to this.pageSize. * Priority: localStorage > @Input pageSize (if valid) > type-specific default. */ private loadPageSizePreference(): void { const stored = this.localStorageService.get(this.pageSizeKey()); const parsed = parseInt(stored, 10); const options = this.pageSizeOptions; if (options.includes(parsed)) { this.pageSize = parsed; return; } // No stored preference: keep parent @Input if it's a valid option if (options.includes(this.pageSize)) { return; } // Neither localStorage nor @Input is valid: use type-specific default this.pageSize = isSavedSearch(this.candidateSource) ? 25 : 10; } /** * Persists the current this.pageSize for the current source. */ private savePageSizePreference(): void { this.localStorageService.set(this.pageSizeKey(), String(this.pageSize)); } ``` `getCandidateSourceType` is already imported (line 46). It returns `'Search'` or `'List'`, so keys become e.g. `Search123PageSize` / `List456PageSize` — matching the cache-service's own key convention. **New event handler** ```typescript /** * Called when the user changes the per-page size selector. * Resets to page 1, persists the preference, and re-fetches. */ onPageSizeChange(size: number): void { this.pageSize = size; this.pageNumber = 1; this.savePageSizePreference(); this.doSearch(true); } ``` **Load preference before first search** In `ngOnChanges`, inside the `changes.candidateSource` block, call `loadPageSizePreference()` _before_ `doSearch(true)`: ```typescript if (changes.candidateSource) { if (changes.candidateSource.previousValue !== changes.candidateSource.currentValue) { if (this.candidateSource) { this.loadSelectedFields(); this.restoreTargetListFromCache(); this.loadPageSizePreference(); // ← NEW (before doSearch) this.doSearch(true); this.selectedCandidates = []; this.loadServiceList(); } } } ``` Why here and not `ngOnInit`? The initial search is triggered from `ngOnChanges` when `candidateSource` arrives as an `@Input` — `ngOnInit` doesn't call `doSearch` directly. If we loaded in `ngOnInit` only, a source change after init would overwrite the preference with undefined before `performSearch` ran. The `searchRequest` change branch does _not_ need `loadPageSizePreference()` because the user is already viewing the same source — page size is unchanged. --- ### 2. `show-candidates.component.html` Add a page-size selector alongside the existing results-summary block. Currently (around line 280) the summary reads: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` Replace the outer `
` (which is currently `*ngIf="!isSavedList()"`) with a layout that always shows the page-size control and conditionally shows the count. The SavedList case currently shows nothing here, so this is non-breaking: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` **Why `[ngValue]` not `[value]`?** The `pageSize` field is a `number`. Using `[value]` would produce a string comparison and the selected option would never match after a localStorage round-trip. `[ngValue]` preserves the number type. **Placement rationale:** Between the filter controls and the table, where pagination concerns naturally live. Users see it before scrolling to the bottom pagination control. --- ## What Could Go Wrong ### 1. `[ngValue]` vs `[value]` type mismatch If `[value]` is used instead of `[ngValue]`, `pageSize` (number) won't match the option values (strings) and the dropdown will always show blank. Fixed by using `[ngValue]` as shown above. ### 2. `pageSize` @Input is actively used by three parents Contrary to the initial research summary, three templates pass `[pageSize]` to `app-show-candidates`: | Caller | Value | |--------|-------| | `candidates-list.component.html` | `[pageSize]="pageSize"` (from URL param, default 20) | | `define-search.component.html` | `[pageSize]="pageSize"` (passed through from its own @Input) | | `view-job-submission-list.component.html` | `[pageSize]="20"` (hardcoded) | All three pass 20, which falls outside both options sets. The `@Input` must be kept to avoid breaking compilation at the call sites. `loadPageSizePreference()` handles the conflict via the priority chain described above: localStorage first, then @Input if valid, then type-specific default. In practice, since 20 is never in the options list, the @Input value is silently superseded by the type-specific default on first load — which is the desired behaviour. ### 3. Corrupt / out-of-range localStorage value The `includes(parsed)` guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` handles this: any value not in the current options set (including `NaN`, old values like 12 or 20, stale options) falls through to the type-specific default — 10 for SavedList, 25 for SavedSearch. ### 4. Page number out of bounds after size change When the user enlarges page size (e.g. from 12 to 50), they may have been on page 4. Resetting `pageNumber = 1` in `onPageSizeChange` prevents the server from receiving a page-number that no longer exists. ### 5. Cache invalidation After a page-size change, `doSearch(true)` is called with `refresh=true`. `checkCache` skips cache reads when `refresh=true`, so the server is always hit. The cache is then repopulated via `cacheResults()` with the new page size. No explicit cache invalidation is needed. --- ## Out of Scope - `CandidateSourceResultsComponent` (browse preview cards, pageSize=12) — a separate context with different UX; not relevant to this ticket - `BrowseCandidateSourcesComponent` (sourceList browser, pageSize=30) — same - Virtual scroll - "Select all across pages" --- ## Todo List ### Phase 1 — TypeScript - [ ] Add `listPageSizeOptions`, `searchPageSizeOptions`, `pageSizeSuffix` fields to `ShowCandidatesComponent` - [ ] Add `pageSizeOptions` getter - [ ] Add `pageSizeKey()` private method - [ ] Add `loadPageSizePreference()` private method (priority: localStorage > @Input > type default) - [ ] Add `savePageSizePreference()` private method - [ ] Add `onPageSizeChange(size: number)` method - [ ] Call `loadPageSizePreference()` in `ngOnChanges` before `doSearch(true)` (source change block only) - [ ] Run typecheck; fix any errors ### Phase 2 — Template - [ ] Replace results-summary block in `show-candidates.component.html` with the new layout containing the page-size dropdown - [ ] Verify the dropdown is visible for both SavedList and SavedSearch sources ### Phase 3 — Test - [ ] Update/extend `show-candidates.component.spec.ts`: - `onPageSizeChange` resets pageNumber to 1 and calls doSearch - `loadPageSizePreference` falls back to 10 (list) / 25 (search) for missing/invalid stored values - `loadPageSizePreference` restores a valid stored value - `savePageSizePreference` writes the correct key/value to localStorage - [ ] Run `ng test` and confirm no regressions ### Phase 4 — Manual verification - [ ] Open a SavedList; change page size; navigate away and back; confirm preference is restored - [ ] Open a SavedSearch; same verification - [ ] Change source mid-session; confirm each source restores its own preference independently - [ ] Verify at 50 and 100 rows: UI is usable and pagination still works

# Plan: Configurable Page Size for Submission Lists (#3045) ## Approach Add a per-source page-size preference stored in `localStorage`, surfaced as a small dropdown in `ShowCandidatesComponent`. The selected value feeds directly into the existing `this.pageSize` field that `performSearch()` already reads, so no new search path is needed. The current effective page size in `ShowCandidatesComponent` is 20 for all entry points — set by callers via `[pageSize]` (from URL params or hardcoded), with the base class fallback of 12 never reached in practice. There is no existing difference between list and search. Going forward we remove those caller inputs and introduce a user-controlled preference with type-specific defaults: | Source type | Options | Default | |-------------|-----------------|---------| | SavedList | 10, 25, 50, 100 | 10 | | SavedSearch | 25, 50, 100 | 25 | No backend changes required — `pageSize` is already part of every paged request (`PagedSearchRequest`). No virtual scroll, no infinite scroll; full-DOM rendering is acceptable up to 100 rows. --- ## Files That Change | File | Nature of change | |------|-----------------| | `show-candidates.component.ts` | New fields, getter, methods; remove `@Input() pageSize` | | `show-candidates.component.html` | Add page-size dropdown; restructure results-summary row | | `candidates-list.component.ts` | Remove `pageSize` field and URL-param read | | `candidates-list.component.html` | Remove `[pageSize]` binding on `app-show-candidates` | | `define-search.component.html` | Remove `[pageSize]` binding on `app-show-candidates` | | `view-job-submission-list.component.html` | Remove `[pageSize]="20"` | --- ### 1. `show-candidates.component.ts` **New constants / fields** ```typescript readonly listPageSizeOptions: number[] = [10, 25, 50, 100]; readonly searchPageSizeOptions: number[] = [25, 50, 100]; private readonly pageSizeSuffix: string = 'PageSize'; get pageSizeOptions(): number[] { return isSavedSearch(this.candidateSource) ? this.searchPageSizeOptions : this.listPageSizeOptions; } ``` The template uses `pageSizeOptions` unchanged; the getter returns the right set based on the current source type. **New private helpers** ```typescript /** * Returns the localStorage key used to persist the page-size preference * for the current candidate source. */ private pageSizeKey(): string { return getCandidateSourceType(this.candidateSource) + this.candidateSource.id + this.pageSizeSuffix; } /** * Reads the persisted page-size preference for the current source and * applies it to this.pageSize, falling back to the type-specific default * if no valid preference is stored. */ private loadPageSizePreference(): void { const stored = this.localStorageService.get(this.pageSizeKey()); const parsed = parseInt(stored, 10); const defaultSize = isSavedSearch(this.candidateSource) ? 25 : 10; this.pageSize = this.pageSizeOptions.includes(parsed) ? parsed : defaultSize; } /** * Persists the current this.pageSize for the current source. */ private savePageSizePreference(): void { this.localStorageService.set(this.pageSizeKey(), String(this.pageSize)); } ``` `getCandidateSourceType` is already imported (line 46). It returns `'Search'` or `'List'`, so keys become e.g. `Search123PageSize` / `List456PageSize` — matching the cache-service's own key convention. **New event handler** ```typescript /** * Called when the user changes the per-page size selector. * Resets to page 1, persists the preference, and re-fetches. */ onPageSizeChange(size: number): void { this.pageSize = size; this.pageNumber = 1; this.savePageSizePreference(); this.doSearch(true); } ``` **Load preference before first search** In `ngOnChanges`, inside the `changes.candidateSource` block, call `loadPageSizePreference()` _before_ `doSearch(true)`: ```typescript if (changes.candidateSource) { if (changes.candidateSource.previousValue !== changes.candidateSource.currentValue) { if (this.candidateSource) { this.loadSelectedFields(); this.restoreTargetListFromCache(); this.loadPageSizePreference(); // ← NEW (before doSearch) this.doSearch(true); this.selectedCandidates = []; this.loadServiceList(); } } } ``` Why here and not `ngOnInit`? The initial search is triggered from `ngOnChanges` when `candidateSource` arrives as an `@Input` — `ngOnInit` doesn't call `doSearch` directly. If we loaded in `ngOnInit` only, a source change after init would overwrite the preference with undefined before `performSearch` ran. The `searchRequest` change branch does _not_ need `loadPageSizePreference()` because the user is already viewing the same source — page size is unchanged. --- ### 2. `show-candidates.component.html` Add a page-size selector alongside the existing results-summary block. Currently (around line 280) the summary reads: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` Replace the outer `
` (which is currently `*ngIf="!isSavedList()"`) with a layout that always shows the page-size control and conditionally shows the count. The SavedList case currently shows nothing here, so this is non-breaking: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` **Why `[ngValue]` not `[value]`?** The `pageSize` field is a `number`. Using `[value]` would produce a string comparison and the selected option would never match after a localStorage round-trip. `[ngValue]` preserves the number type. **Placement rationale:** Between the filter controls and the table, where pagination concerns naturally live. Users see it before scrolling to the bottom pagination control. --- ## What Could Go Wrong ### 1. `[ngValue]` vs `[value]` type mismatch If `[value]` is used instead of `[ngValue]`, `pageSize` (number) won't match the option values (strings) and the dropdown will always show blank. Fixed by using `[ngValue]` as shown above. ### 2. Removing `pageSize` from callers Three templates previously passed `[pageSize]` to `app-show-candidates` and are cleaned up as part of this ticket: | File | Change | |------|--------| | `candidates-list.component.html` | Remove `[pageSize]="pageSize"` | | `candidates-list.component.ts` | Remove `pageSize` field and URL-param read — it was only used to feed show-candidates | | `define-search.component.html` | Remove `[pageSize]="pageSize"` from `app-show-candidates` only — define-search's own `@Input() pageSize` and its use at line 419 (`request.pageSize = this.pageSize`) are unrelated to show-candidates and must stay | | `view-job-submission-list.component.html` | Remove `[pageSize]="20"` | `show-candidates.component.ts`: remove `@Input() declare pageSize: number` — `pageSize` becomes a plain instance variable initialized solely by `loadPageSizePreference()`. ### 3. Corrupt / out-of-range localStorage value The `includes(parsed)` guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` handles this: any value not in the current options set (including `NaN`, old values like 12 or 20, stale options) falls through to the type-specific default — 10 for SavedList, 25 for SavedSearch. ### 4. Page number out of bounds after size change When the user enlarges page size (e.g. from 12 to 50), they may have been on page 4. Resetting `pageNumber = 1` in `onPageSizeChange` prevents the server from receiving a page-number that no longer exists. ### 5. Cache invalidation After a page-size change, `doSearch(true)` is called with `refresh=true`. `checkCache` skips cache reads when `refresh=true`, so the server is always hit. The cache is then repopulated via `cacheResults()` with the new page size. No explicit cache invalidation is needed. --- ## Out of Scope - `CandidateSourceResultsComponent` (browse preview cards, pageSize=12) — a separate context with different UX; not relevant to this ticket - `BrowseCandidateSourcesComponent` (sourceList browser, pageSize=30) — same - Virtual scroll - "Select all across pages" --- ## Todo List ### Phase 1 — TypeScript - [ ] Remove `@Input() declare pageSize: number` from `ShowCandidatesComponent`; keep `pageSize` as plain field - [ ] Add `listPageSizeOptions`, `searchPageSizeOptions`, `pageSizeSuffix` fields - [ ] Add `pageSizeOptions` getter - [ ] Add `pageSizeKey()` private method - [ ] Add `loadPageSizePreference()` private method (localStorage or type-specific default) - [ ] Add `savePageSizePreference()` private method - [ ] Add `onPageSizeChange(size: number)` method - [ ] Call `loadPageSizePreference()` in `ngOnChanges` before `doSearch(true)` (source change block only) - [ ] Remove `pageSize` field and URL-param read from `candidates-list.component.ts` - [ ] Run typecheck; fix any errors ### Phase 2 — Templates - [ ] Replace results-summary block in `show-candidates.component.html` with new layout containing page-size dropdown - [ ] Remove `[pageSize]="pageSize"` from `candidates-list.component.html` - [ ] Remove `[pageSize]="pageSize"` from `define-search.component.html` - [ ] Remove `[pageSize]="20"` from `view-job-submission-list.component.html` ### Phase 3 — Test - [ ] Update/extend `show-candidates.component.spec.ts`: - `onPageSizeChange` resets pageNumber to 1 and calls doSearch - `loadPageSizePreference` falls back to 10 (list) / 25 (search) for missing/invalid stored values - `loadPageSizePreference` restores a valid stored value - `savePageSizePreference` writes the correct key/value to localStorage - [ ] Run `ng test` and confirm no regressions ### Phase 4 — Manual verification - [ ] Open a SavedList; change page size; navigate away and back; confirm preference is restored - [ ] Open a SavedSearch; same verification - [ ] Change source mid-session; confirm each source restores its own preference independently - [ ] Verify at 50 and 100 rows: UI is usable and pagination still works

message.content: Finally, what's the probable cost of including 200 and even 500? Might it be worth it?

content.text:
Three concrete costs, in order of severity:

**1. localStorage quota — hard limit, not just slowness.**
The cache service writes the full page of `EXTENDED` candidate objects to localStorage. At ~50–100 KB per candidate: 200 candidates ≈ 10–20 MB, 500 candidates ≈ 25–50 MB. Browser localStorage limits are typically 5–10 MB per origin. `setItem` will throw a `QuotaExceededError`. Whether the cache service handles that gracefully I'd need to check, but even if it does, caching silently stops working and users get a server hit on every navigation. For 500 this is essentially guaranteed to fail.

**2. DOM size — noticeable but not catastrophic at 200.**
Each row has ~20–30 bindings and event listeners. At 200 rows, initial render and Angular's change detection sweep will be perceptibly slow on average hardware (think 500–1500ms). At 500 it becomes genuinely bad — scrolling jank, delayed selection feedback. No virtual scroll means the full DOM sits in memory.

**3. Payload — large but manageable with a good connection.**
200 × 50–100 KB ≈ 10–20 MB per request; 500 ≈ 25–50 MB. On a fast connection that's tolerable latency-wise, but mobile or slow office connections would time out or stall noticeably.

**Is it worth it?**
For 200: probably not without first disabling the localStorage cache for large page sizes (fallback to always hitting the server). That's a small targeted change to the cache service.

For 500: no, not without virtual scroll and dropping the localStorage cache entirely at that scale. The architectural cost exceeds the UX benefit, especially given there's still no "select all" — a user scrolling 500 rows to individually tick candidates is worse than just paginating.

My recommendation: cap at 100 for now. If users ask for more, the next step is "select all on page" combined with cross-page bulk operations — that's the real ask behind wanting 500 rows visible.

# Plan: Configurable Page Size for Submission Lists (#3045) ## Approach Add a per-source page-size preference stored in `localStorage`, surfaced as a small dropdown in `ShowCandidatesComponent`. The selected value feeds directly into the existing `this.pageSize` field that `performSearch()` already reads, so no new search path is needed. The current effective page size in `ShowCandidatesComponent` is 20 for all entry points — set by callers via `[pageSize]` (from URL params or hardcoded), with the base class fallback of 12 never reached in practice. There is no existing difference between list and search. Going forward we introduce a user-controlled preference with a single shared option set for both source types, while keeping the `@Input() pageSize` typed to only accept valid values: | Options | Default | |--------------|---------| | 20, 50, 100 | 20 | A single option set eliminates the need for separate list/search arrays and any source-type branching in the preference logic. All existing callers (which pass 20) remain valid with no changes required to caller files. No backend changes required — `pageSize` is already part of every paged request (`PagedSearchRequest`). No virtual scroll, no infinite scroll; full-DOM rendering is acceptable up to 100 rows. --- ## Files That Change | File | Nature of change | |------|-----------------| | `show-candidates.component.ts` | Type `@Input() pageSize`; add options, getter, methods | | `show-candidates.component.html` | Add page-size dropdown; restructure results-summary row | --- ### 1. `show-candidates.component.ts` **Type alias and updated @Input** ```typescript export type CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100; // Replace existing: @Input() declare pageSize: number; // With: @Input() pageSize: CandidatePageSize; ``` **New constants / fields** ```typescript readonly pageSizeOptions: CandidatePageSize[] = [20, 50, 100]; private readonly pageSizeSuffix: string = 'PageSize'; ``` **New private helpers** ```typescript /** * Returns the localStorage key used to persist the page-size preference * for the current candidate source. */ private pageSizeKey(): string { return getCandidateSourceType(this.candidateSource) + this.candidateSource.id + this.pageSizeSuffix; } /** * Reads the persisted page-size preference for the current source and * applies it to this.pageSize. * Priority: localStorage > @Input pageSize (if valid) > 20. */ private loadPageSizePreference(): void { const stored = this.localStorageService.get(this.pageSizeKey()); const parsed = parseInt(stored, 10) as CandidatePageSize; if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(parsed)) { this.pageSize = parsed; return; } if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(this.pageSize)) { return; // @Input value is valid — keep it } this.pageSize = 20; } /** * Persists the current this.pageSize for the current source. */ private savePageSizePreference(): void { this.localStorageService.set(this.pageSizeKey(), String(this.pageSize)); } ``` `getCandidateSourceType` is already imported (line 46). It returns `'Search'` or `'List'`, so keys become e.g. `Search123PageSize` / `List456PageSize` — matching the cache-service's own key convention. **New event handler** ```typescript /** * Called when the user changes the per-page size selector. * Resets to page 1, persists the preference, and re-fetches. */ onPageSizeChange(size: number): void { this.pageSize = size; this.pageNumber = 1; this.savePageSizePreference(); this.doSearch(true); } ``` **Load preference before first search** In `ngOnChanges`, inside the `changes.candidateSource` block, call `loadPageSizePreference()` _before_ `doSearch(true)`: ```typescript if (changes.candidateSource) { if (changes.candidateSource.previousValue !== changes.candidateSource.currentValue) { if (this.candidateSource) { this.loadSelectedFields(); this.restoreTargetListFromCache(); this.loadPageSizePreference(); // ← NEW (before doSearch) this.doSearch(true); this.selectedCandidates = []; this.loadServiceList(); } } } ``` Why here and not `ngOnInit`? The initial search is triggered from `ngOnChanges` when `candidateSource` arrives as an `@Input` — `ngOnInit` doesn't call `doSearch` directly. If we loaded in `ngOnInit` only, a source change after init would overwrite the preference with undefined before `performSearch` ran. The `searchRequest` change branch does _not_ need `loadPageSizePreference()` because the user is already viewing the same source — page size is unchanged. --- ### 2. `show-candidates.component.html` Add a page-size selector alongside the existing results-summary block. Currently (around line 280) the summary reads: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` Replace the outer `
` (which is currently `*ngIf="!isSavedList()"`) with a layout that always shows the page-size control and conditionally shows the count. The SavedList case currently shows nothing here, so this is non-breaking: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` **Why `[ngValue]` not `[value]`?** The `pageSize` field is a `number`. Using `[value]` would produce a string comparison and the selected option would never match after a localStorage round-trip. `[ngValue]` preserves the number type. **Placement rationale:** Between the filter controls and the table, where pagination concerns naturally live. Users see it before scrolling to the bottom pagination control. --- ## What Could Go Wrong ### 1. `[ngValue]` vs `[value]` type mismatch If `[value]` is used instead of `[ngValue]`, `pageSize` (number) won't match the option values (strings) and the dropdown will always show blank. Fixed by using `[ngValue]` as shown above. ### 2. `@Input() pageSize` type correctness `CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100` exactly matches the option set. Any out-of-range value (e.g. a future caller passing an unlisted number) will be caught by TypeScript at compile time. The runtime guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` covers values arriving from localStorage that predate an option-set change. ### 3. Corrupt / out-of-range localStorage value The `includes(parsed)` guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` handles this: any value not in the current options set (including `NaN`, old values like 12 or 25, stale options) falls through to the @Input check and then the type-specific default — 10 for SavedList, 20 for SavedSearch. ### 4. Page number out of bounds after size change When the user enlarges page size (e.g. from 12 to 50), they may have been on page 4. Resetting `pageNumber = 1` in `onPageSizeChange` prevents the server from receiving a page-number that no longer exists. ### 5. Cache invalidation After a page-size change, `doSearch(true)` is called with `refresh=true`. `checkCache` skips cache reads when `refresh=true`, so the server is always hit. The cache is then repopulated via `cacheResults()` with the new page size. No explicit cache invalidation is needed. --- ## Out of Scope - `CandidateSourceResultsComponent` (browse preview cards, pageSize=12) — a separate context with different UX; not relevant to this ticket - `BrowseCandidateSourcesComponent` (sourceList browser, pageSize=30) — same - Virtual scroll - "Select all across pages" --- ## Todo List ### Phase 1 — TypeScript - [ ] Define `CandidatePageSize` type alias; type `@Input() pageSize` with it - [ ] Add `listPageSizeOptions`, `searchPageSizeOptions`, `pageSizeSuffix` fields - [ ] Add `pageSizeOptions` getter - [ ] Add `pageSizeKey()` private method - [ ] Add `loadPageSizePreference()` private method (localStorage > @Input > type-specific default) - [ ] Add `savePageSizePreference()` private method - [ ] Add `onPageSizeChange(size: CandidatePageSize)` method - [ ] Call `loadPageSizePreference()` in `ngOnChanges` before `doSearch(true)` (source change block only) - [ ] Run typecheck; fix any errors ### Phase 2 — Template - [ ] Replace results-summary block in `show-candidates.component.html` with new layout containing page-size dropdown ### Phase 3 — Test - [ ] Update/extend `show-candidates.component.spec.ts`: - `onPageSizeChange` resets pageNumber to 1 and calls doSearch - `loadPageSizePreference` falls back to 10 (list) / 20 (search) for missing/invalid stored values - `loadPageSizePreference` restores a valid stored value - `savePageSizePreference` writes the correct key/value to localStorage - [ ] Run `ng test` and confirm no regressions ### Phase 4 — Manual verification - [ ] Open a SavedList; change page size; navigate away and back; confirm preference is restored - [ ] Open a SavedSearch; same verification - [ ] Change source mid-session; confirm each source restores its own preference independently - [ ] Verify at 50 and 100 rows: UI is usable and pagination still works

The current effective page size in `ShowCandidatesComponent` is 20 for all entry points — set by callers via `[pageSize]` (from URL params or hardcoded), with the base class fallback of 12 never reached in practice. There is no existing difference between list and search. Going forward we introduce a user-controlled preference with a single shared option set for both source types, while keeping the `@Input() pageSize` typed to only accept valid values: | Options | Default | |--------------|---------| | 20, 50, 100 | 20 | A single option set eliminates the need for separate list/search arrays and any source-type branching in the preference logic. All existing callers (which pass 20) remain valid with no changes required to caller files. No backend changes required — `pageSize` is already part of every paged request (`PagedSearchRequest`). No virtual scroll, no infinite scroll; full-DOM rendering is acceptable up to 100 rows. --- ## Files That Change | File | Nature of change | |------|-----------------| | `show-candidates.component.ts` | Type `@Input() pageSize`; add options, getter, methods | | `show-candidates.component.html` | Add page-size dropdown; restructure results-summary row | --- ### 1. `show-candidates.component.ts` **Type alias and updated @Input** ```typescript export type CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100; // Replace existing: @Input() declare pageSize: number; // With: @Input() pageSize: CandidatePageSize; ``` **New constants / fields** ```typescript readonly pageSizeOptions: CandidatePageSize[] = [20, 50, 100]; ``` **New private helpers** ```typescript /** * Returns the localStorage key used to persist the page-size preference * for the current candidate source. */ private pageSizeKey(): string { return getCandidateSourceType(this.candidateSource) + this.candidateSource.id + this.pageSizeSuffix; } /** * Reads the persisted page-size preference for the current source and * applies it to this.pageSize. * Priority: localStorage > @Input pageSize (if valid) > 20. */ private loadPageSizePreference(): void { const stored = this.localStorageService.get(this.pageSizeKey()); const parsed = parseInt(stored, 10) as CandidatePageSize; if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(parsed)) { this.pageSize = parsed; return; } if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(this.pageSize)) { return; // @Input value is valid — keep it } this.pageSize = 20; } /** * Persists the current this.pageSize for the current source. */ private savePageSizePreference(): void { this.localStorageService.set(this.pageSizeKey(), String(this.pageSize)); } ``` `getCandidateSourceType` is already imported (line 46). The initial search is triggered from `ngOnChanges` when `candidateSource` arrives as an `@Input` — `ngOnInit` doesn't call `doSearch` directly. If we loaded in `ngOnInit` only, a source change after init would overwrite the preference with undefined before `performSearch` ran. {{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` Replace the outer `

{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}

content.text: Done.

It reads the stored preference from localStorage, parses it as a number, then works through three cases in priority order:

1. **localStorage has a valid value** — use it. This is the common case once a user has made a choice.

2. **localStorage is empty or invalid, but `this.pageSize` is already valid** — do nothing. This covers the first visit to a source: the `@Input` has set `this.pageSize` to 20 before `loadPageSizePreference()` runs, 20 is in the options list, so we keep it.

3. **Neither is valid** — fall back to 20. This covers stale localStorage values (e.g. a value from before this feature existed) where the `@Input` also wasn't provided or was out of range.

One thing worth noting: the `as CandidatePageSize` cast on line 2 is a lie — `parseInt` returns `number`, and if the stored string is `"42"` or `"NaN"`, the cast doesn't actually make it a valid `CandidatePageSize` at runtime. The `includes` check on line 3 is what actually enforces validity. The cast just stops TypeScript complaining about passing a `number` to `includes` on a `CandidatePageSize[]`. It's harmless but slightly misleading — worth knowing it's there for the compiler, not for safety.

content.text: Yes. `LocalStorageService.set` serializes to string — localStorage only stores strings. So `savePageSizePreference` writes `"20"`, `"50"`, or `"100"`, and `parseInt` in `loadPageSizePreference` converts it back to a number.

content.text:
No — `tc-dropdown` is an action menu, not a value picker. `tc-dropdown-item` emits `(itemSelect): void` with no concept of a selected state or two-way binding. You could wire it up manually, but you'd be building a custom select on top of an action menu: tracking which item is active, styling it as selected, handling keyboard navigation yourself. That's more complexity than it's worth.

The native `<select class="form-select form-select-sm">` is the right tool — it naturally shows the current value, has built-in keyboard support, and binds cleanly with `[ngModel]`. It's also already used elsewhere in the same template (the review status filter uses `ng-select`). No reason to reach for `tc-dropdown` here.

message.content: Ah okay, how about an ng-select with the class decorator tc-select - I believe that's the convention elsewhere.

content.text:
Yes, that's the pattern — already used twice in the same template. For a simple single-value number picker it would be:

```html
<ng-select class="tc-select"
           [items]="pageSizeOptions"
           [searchable]="false"
           [clearable]="false"
           [ngModel]="pageSize"
           (ngModelChange)="onPageSizeChange($event)">
</ng-select>
```

No `bindLabel` or `bindValue` needed since the items are plain primitives. `[clearable]="false"` is important — there's no valid "no selection" state for page size. `[searchable]="false"` since there are only three options.

The current effective page size in `ShowCandidatesComponent` is 20 for all entry points — set by callers via `[pageSize]` (from URL params or hardcoded), with the base class fallback of 12 never reached in practice. There is no existing difference between list and search. Going forward we introduce a user-controlled preference with a single shared option set for both source types, while keeping the `@Input() pageSize` typed to only accept valid values: | Options | Default | |--------------|---------| | 20, 50, 100 | 20 | A single option set eliminates the need for separate list/search arrays and any source-type branching in the preference logic. All existing callers (which pass 20) remain valid with no changes required to caller files. No backend changes required — `pageSize` is already part of every paged request (`PagedSearchRequest`). No virtual scroll, no infinite scroll; full-DOM rendering is acceptable up to 100 rows. --- ## Files That Change | File | Nature of change | |------|-----------------| | `show-candidates.component.ts` | Type `@Input() pageSize`; add options, getter, methods | | `show-candidates.component.html` | Add page-size dropdown; restructure results-summary row | --- ### 1. `show-candidates.component.ts` **Type alias and updated @Input** ```typescript export type CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100; // Replace existing: @Input() declare pageSize: number; // With: @Input() pageSize: CandidatePageSize; ``` **New constants / fields** ```typescript readonly pageSizeOptions: CandidatePageSize[] = [20, 50, 100]; ``` **New private helpers** ```typescript /** * Returns the localStorage key used to persist the page-size preference * for the current candidate source. */ private pageSizeKey(): string { return getCandidateSourceType(this.candidateSource) + this.candidateSource.id + 'PageSize'; } /** * Reads the persisted page-size preference for the current source and * applies it to this.pageSize. * Priority: localStorage > @Input pageSize (if valid) > 20. */ private loadPageSizePreference(): void { const stored = this.localStorageService.get(this.pageSizeKey()); const parsed = parseInt(stored, 10) as CandidatePageSize; if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(parsed)) { this.pageSize = parsed; return; } if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(this.pageSize)) { return; // @Input value is valid — keep it } this.pageSize = 20; } /** * Persists the current this.pageSize for the current source. */ private savePageSizePreference(): void { this.localStorageService.set(this.pageSizeKey(), String(this.pageSize)); } ``` `getCandidateSourceType` is already imported (line 46). It returns `'Search'` or `'List'`, so keys become e.g. `Search123PageSize` / `List456PageSize` — matching the cache-service's own key convention. **New event handler** ```typescript /** * Called when the user changes the per-page size selector. * Resets to page 1, persists the preference, and re-fetches. */ onPageSizeChange(size: number): void { this.pageSize = size; this.pageNumber = 1; this.savePageSizePreference(); this.doSearch(true); } ``` **Load preference before first search** In `ngOnChanges`, inside the `changes.candidateSource` block, call `loadPageSizePreference()` _before_ `doSearch(true)`: ```typescript if (changes.candidateSource) { if (changes.candidateSource.previousValue !== changes.candidateSource.currentValue) { if (this.candidateSource) { this.loadSelectedFields(); this.restoreTargetListFromCache(); this.loadPageSizePreference(); // ← NEW (before doSearch) this.doSearch(true); this.selectedCandidates = []; this.loadServiceList(); } } } ``` Why here and not `ngOnInit`? The initial search is triggered from `ngOnChanges` when `candidateSource` arrives as an `@Input` — `ngOnInit` doesn't call `doSearch` directly. If we loaded in `ngOnInit` only, a source change after init would overwrite the preference with undefined before `performSearch` ran. The `searchRequest` change branch does _not_ need `loadPageSizePreference()` because the user is already viewing the same source — page size is unchanged. --- ### 2. `show-candidates.component.html` Add a page-size selector alongside the existing results-summary block. Currently (around line 280) the summary reads: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` Replace the outer `
` (which is currently `*ngIf="!isSavedList()"`) with a layout that always shows the page-size control and conditionally shows the count. The SavedList case currently shows nothing here, so this is non-breaking: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` **Placement rationale:** Between the filter controls and the table, where pagination concerns naturally live. Users see it before scrolling to the bottom pagination control. --- ## What Could Go Wrong ### 1. `@Input() pageSize` type correctness `CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100` exactly matches the option set. Any out-of-range value (e.g. a future caller passing an unlisted number) will be caught by TypeScript at compile time. The runtime guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` covers values arriving from localStorage that predate an option-set change. ### 3. Corrupt / out-of-range localStorage value The `includes(parsed)` guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` handles this: any value not in `[20, 50, 100]` (including `NaN`, old values like 12 or 10, stale options) falls through to the @Input check and then the default of 20. ### 4. Page number out of bounds after size change When the user enlarges page size (e.g. from 20 to 50), they may have been on page 4. Resetting `pageNumber = 1` in `onPageSizeChange` prevents the server from receiving a page-number that no longer exists. ### 5. Cache invalidation After a page-size change, `doSearch(true)` is called with `refresh=true`. `checkCache` skips cache reads when `refresh=true`, so the server is always hit. The cache is then repopulated via `cacheResults()` with the new page size. No explicit cache invalidation is needed. --- ## Out of Scope - `CandidateSourceResultsComponent` (browse preview cards, pageSize=12) — a separate context with different UX; not relevant to this ticket - `BrowseCandidateSourcesComponent` (sourceList browser, pageSize=30) — same - Virtual scroll - "Select all across pages" --- ## Todo List ### Phase 1 — TypeScript - [ ] Define `CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100`; type `@Input() pageSize` with it - [ ] Add `pageSizeOptions` field - [ ] Add `pageSizeKey()` private method - [ ] Add `loadPageSizePreference()` private method (localStorage > @Input > 20) - [ ] Add `savePageSizePreference()` private method - [ ] Add `onPageSizeChange(size: CandidatePageSize)` method - [ ] Call `loadPageSizePreference()` in `ngOnChanges` before `doSearch(true)` (source change block only) - [ ] Run typecheck; fix any errors ### Phase 2 — Template - [ ] Replace results-summary block in `show-candidates.component.html` with new layout containing page-size dropdown ### Phase 3 — Test - [ ] Update/extend `show-candidates.component.spec.ts`: - `onPageSizeChange` resets pageNumber to 1 and calls doSearch - `loadPageSizePreference` falls back to 20 for missing/invalid stored values - `loadPageSizePreference` restores a valid stored value - `savePageSizePreference` writes the correct key/value to localStorage - [ ] Run `ng test` and confirm no regressions ### Phase 4 — Manual verification - [ ] Open a SavedList; change page size; navigate away and back; confirm preference is restored - [ ] Open a SavedSearch; same verification - [ ] Change source mid-session; confirm each source restores its own preference independently - [ ] Verify at 50 and 100 rows: UI is usable and pagination still works

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Plan: Configurable Page Size for Submission Lists (#3045) ## Approach Add a per-source page-size preference stored in `localStorage`, surfaced as a small dropdown in `ShowCandidatesComponent`. The selected value feeds directly into the existing `this.pageSize` field that `performSearch()` already reads, so no new search path is needed. The current effective page size in `ShowCandidatesComponent` is 20 for all entry points — set by callers via `[pageSize]` (from URL params or hardcoded), with the base class fallback of 12 never reached in practice. There is no existing difference between list and search. Going forward we introduce a user-controlled preference with a single shared option set for both source types, while keeping the `@Input() pageSize` typed to only accept valid values: | Options | Default | |--------------|---------| | 20, 50, 100 | 20 | A single option set eliminates the need for separate list/search arrays and any source-type branching in the preference logic. All existing callers (which pass 20) remain valid with no changes required to caller files. No backend changes required — `pageSize` is already part of every paged request (`PagedSearchRequest`). No virtual scroll, no infinite scroll; full-DOM rendering is acceptable up to 100 rows. --- ## Files That Change | File | Nature of change | |------|-----------------| | `show-candidates.component.ts` | Type `@Input() pageSize`; add options, getter, methods | | `show-candidates.component.html` | Add page-size dropdown; restructure results-summary row | --- ### 1. `show-candidates.component.ts` **Type alias and updated @Input** ```typescript export type CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100; // Replace existing: @Input() declare pageSize: number; // With: @Input() pageSize: CandidatePageSize; ``` **New constants / fields** ```typescript readonly pageSizeOptions: CandidatePageSize[] = [20, 50, 100]; ``` **New private helpers** ```typescript /** * Returns the localStorage key used to persist the page-size preference * for the current candidate source. */ private pageSizeKey(): string { return getCandidateSourceType(this.candidateSource) + this.candidateSource.id + 'PageSize'; } /** * Reads the persisted page-size preference for the current source and * applies it to this.pageSize. * Priority: localStorage > @Input pageSize (if valid) > 20. */ private loadPageSizePreference(): void { const stored = this.localStorageService.get(this.pageSizeKey()); const parsed = parseInt(stored, 10) as CandidatePageSize; if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(parsed)) { this.pageSize = parsed; return; } if (this.pageSizeOptions.includes(this.pageSize)) { return; // @Input value is valid — keep it } this.pageSize = 20; } /** * Persists the current this.pageSize for the current source. */ private savePageSizePreference(): void { this.localStorageService.set(this.pageSizeKey(), String(this.pageSize)); } ``` `getCandidateSourceType` is already imported (line 46). It returns `'Search'` or `'List'`, so keys become e.g. `Search123PageSize` / `List456PageSize` — matching the cache-service's own key convention. **New event handler** ```typescript /** * Called when the user changes the per-page size selector. * Resets to page 1, persists the preference, and re-fetches. */ onPageSizeChange(size: number): void { this.pageSize = size; this.pageNumber = 1; this.savePageSizePreference(); this.doSearch(true); } ``` **Load preference before first search** In `ngOnChanges`, inside the `changes.candidateSource` block, call `loadPageSizePreference()` _before_ `doSearch(true)`: ```typescript if (changes.candidateSource) { if (changes.candidateSource.previousValue !== changes.candidateSource.currentValue) { if (this.candidateSource) { this.loadSelectedFields(); this.restoreTargetListFromCache(); this.loadPageSizePreference(); // ← NEW (before doSearch) this.doSearch(true); this.selectedCandidates = []; this.loadServiceList(); } } } ``` Why here and not `ngOnInit`? The initial search is triggered from `ngOnChanges` when `candidateSource` arrives as an `@Input` — `ngOnInit` doesn't call `doSearch` directly. If we loaded in `ngOnInit` only, a source change after init would overwrite the preference with undefined before `performSearch` ran. The `searchRequest` change branch does _not_ need `loadPageSizePreference()` because the user is already viewing the same source — page size is unchanged. --- ### 2. `show-candidates.component.html` Add a page-size selector alongside the existing results-summary block. Currently (around line 280) the summary reads: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` Replace the outer `
` (which is currently `*ngIf="!isSavedList()"`) with a layout that always shows the page-size control and conditionally shows the count. The SavedList case currently shows nothing here, so this is non-breaking: ```html
{{results?.totalElements}} candidates returned
{{timestamp | date: 'customDateTime'}}
``` **Placement rationale:** Between the filter controls and the table, where pagination concerns naturally live. Users see it before scrolling to the bottom pagination control. --- ## What Could Go Wrong ### 1. `@Input() pageSize` type correctness `CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100` exactly matches the option set. Any out-of-range value (e.g. a future caller passing an unlisted number) will be caught by TypeScript at compile time. The runtime guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` covers values arriving from localStorage that predate an option-set change. ### 3. Corrupt / out-of-range localStorage value The `includes(parsed)` guard in `loadPageSizePreference()` handles this: any value not in `[20, 50, 100]` (including `NaN`, old values like 12 or 10, stale options) falls through to the @Input check and then the default of 20. ### 4. Page number out of bounds after size change When the user enlarges page size (e.g. from 20 to 50), they may have been on page 4. Resetting `pageNumber = 1` in `onPageSizeChange` prevents the server from receiving a page-number that no longer exists. ### 5. Cache invalidation After a page-size change, `doSearch(true)` is called with `refresh=true`. `checkCache` skips cache reads when `refresh=true`, so the server is always hit. The cache is then repopulated via `cacheResults()` with the new page size. No explicit cache invalidation is needed. --- ## Out of Scope - `CandidateSourceResultsComponent` (browse preview cards, pageSize=12) — a separate context with different UX; not relevant to this ticket - `BrowseCandidateSourcesComponent` (sourceList browser, pageSize=30) — same - Virtual scroll - "Select all across pages" --- ## Todo List ### Phase 1 — TypeScript - [ ] Define `CandidatePageSize = 20 | 50 | 100`; type `@Input() pageSize` with it - [ ] Add `pageSizeOptions` field - [ ] Add `pageSizeKey()` private method - [ ] Add `loadPageSizePreference()` private method (localStorage > @Input > 20) - [ ] Add `savePageSizePreference()` private method - [ ] Add `onPageSizeChange(size: CandidatePageSize)` method - [ ] Call `loadPageSizePreference()` in `ngOnChanges` before `doSearch(true)` (source change block only) - [ ] Run typecheck; fix any errors ### Phase 2 — Template - [ ] Replace results-summary block in `show-candidates.component.html` with new layout containing page-size dropdown ### Phase 3 — Test - [ ] Update/extend `show-candidates.component.spec.ts`: - `onPageSizeChange` resets pageNumber to 1 and calls doSearch - `loadPageSizePreference` falls back to 20 for missing/invalid stored values - `loadPageSizePreference` restores a valid stored value - `savePageSizePreference` writes the correct key/value to localStorage - [ ] Run `ng test` and confirm no regressions ### Phase 4 — Manual verification - [ ] Open a SavedList; change page size; navigate away and back; confirm preference is restored - [ ] Open a SavedSearch; same verification - [ ] Change source mid-session; confirm each source restores its own preference independently - [ ] Verify at 50 and 100 rows: UI is usable and pagination still works

message.content: Just curious (don't implement anything) - what would it take to add it to the ngbpagination?

content.text:
`NgbPagination` has no built-in page-size slot — it only handles page navigation. So "adding it to NgbPagination" really means adding it adjacent to NgbPagination inside `tc-table`'s template.

That would require:
1. Adding `@Input() pageSizeOptions` and `@Input() pageSize` to `tc-table`
2. Adding `@Output() pageSizeChange` to emit the selection upward
3. Placing the `ng-select` next to the `<ngb-pagination>` in `tc-table`'s template
4. Wiring `(pageSizeChange)="onPageSizeChange($event)"` at every `<tc-table>` call site

The result would be a cleaner UX — the selector lives right next to the pagination controls at both top and bottom of the table (since `tc-table` renders pagination in both positions) — but it would mean touching `tc-table` and every component that uses it, which is why it was ruled out early. The current placement is a pragmatic workaround for that constraint.
